commands.install: TS=/tmp/bsf-truststore.p12; CA="$(dirname "$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$(command -v java)")")")/lib/security/cacerts"; if [ ! -s "$TS" ] && [ -r "$CA" ]; then cp "$CA" "$TS"; fi; if [ ! -s "$TS" ]; then D="$(mktemp -d)"; csplit -sz -f "$D/c" -b "%03d.pem" /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt '/BEGIN CERTIFICATE/' '{*}'; for f in "$D"/c*.pem; do keytool -importcert -noprompt -trustcacerts -alias "$(basename "$f" .pem)" -file "$f" -keystore "$TS" -storetype PKCS12 -storepass changeit >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; done; rm -rf "$D"; fi; mvn -B -ntp -DskipTests dependency:resolve
commands.coverage:
rm -rf target/coverage target/site/jacoco && mvn -B -ntp org.jacoco:jacoco-maven-plugin:0.8.16:prepare-agent test org.jacoco:jacoco-maven-plugin:0.8.16:report && python3 -I - target/site/jacoco/jacoco.xml target/coverage/lcov.info <<'PY'
import os, sys, xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
index = {}
for root, dirs, files in os.walk("."):
    dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in (".git", "target", "build", "node_modules")]
    for f in files:
        index.setdefault(f, []).append(os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, f), ".").replace(os.sep, "/"))
out = []
for pkg in ET.parse(src).getroot().iter("package"):
    pkgdir = pkg.get("name", "")
    for sf in pkg.iter("sourcefile"):
        name = sf.get("name", "")
        want = "%s/%s" % (pkgdir, name) if pkgdir else name
        hits = [p for p in index.get(name, []) if p.endswith(want)]
        path = hits[0] if hits else "src/main/java/" + want
        lines = [(int(l.get("nr", "0")), int(l.get("ci", "0")), int(l.get("mb", "0")), int(l.get("cb", "0"))) for l in sf.iter("line")]
        if not lines:
            continue
        out.append("SF:" + path)
        for nr, ci, mb, cb in lines:
            out.append("DA:%d,%d" % (nr, ci))
            for i in range(mb + cb):
                out.append("BRDA:%d,0,%d,%d" % (nr, i, 1 if i < cb else 0))
        out.append("LF:%d" % len(lines))
        out.append("LH:%d" % sum(1 for _, ci, _, _ in lines if ci > 0))
        out.append("end_of_record")
if not out:
    sys.exit("no sourcefile line data in " + src)
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dst) or ".", exist_ok=True)
open(dst, "w").write("\n".join(out) + "\n")
print("wrote %s: %d file(s)" % (dst, sum(1 for l in out if l.startswith("SF:"))))
PY

env.name: SERVER_PORT
env.why: The port Spring Boot binds. The app reads no configuration of its own, so this is Spring's own default made explicit, and it is the port app_url and the runbook use.

env.name: MAVEN_OPTS
env.why: Build configuration, not app configuration. Two facts about the sandbox made it necessary: the agent container's HOME/.m2 is root-owned, so Maven cannot create its default local repository, and its JDK truststore is a dangling symlink (/etc/ssl/certs/adoptium is absent), so every HTTPS fetch from Maven Central failed with 'trustAnchors parameter must be non-empty'. The install command puts a valid PKCS12 truststore at that path — copied from the JDK's own cacerts where it is readable, otherwise built from /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt — so the same commands work on the runner and in an agent container. No credential: changeit is the stock truststore password and a truststore holds public CA certificates only.

dropped.why: Actions plumbing for a hosted runner, not something the app needs installed. The sandbox uses the JDK already on PATH and its own local repository under /tmp; pinning a JDK here would describe CI rather than the app.
Carried over, but without -q: the trial and the roles read command output to tell a pass from a silent failure, so quiet mode is dropped and -ntp used instead to keep the log short.

exercised: The whole build: mvn package compiles src/main/java and repackages the Spring Boot fat jar (target/loans-0.1.0.jar).
The whole test suite: 3 JUnit 5 tests in src/test/java (LoanTest, LoanControllerTest), run by surefire.
The app running: mvn spring-boot:run starts the embedded Tomcat and GET /loans/overdue answers 200 with the JSON list within ~5s of a warm local repository.
The HTTP contract of GET /loans/overdue, with and without the ?on= parameter, including ordering (most overdue first) and the daysLate field.
A browser loading that URL: Chromium renders the JSON response, so a visual check of the endpoint is possible.
Changes to the overdue rule (Loan.overdueOn / Loan.daysLate), to the controller's mapping and response shape, and to the tests.

Line coverage of the main sources: the same 3 tests run under the JaCoCo agent, the XML report converted to lcov at target/coverage/lcov.info. 3 files, 15 of 18 lines (83.3%) with the tests as they stand; LoansApplication.main is the uncovered part.

javac's own -Xlint:all warnings over src/main and src/test, as SARIF at target/static/javac.sarif. Clean on the repo as it stands (0 findings), and it fires on the rule pack's own bad examples: 3 rawtypes, 1 unchecked and 1 fallthrough.

not_exercised.what: Any storage. The loan list is a hard-coded List.of in the controller, so nothing here exercises a database, a migration or persistence of any kind, and no service is started.
not_exercised.why: The repo has no persistence layer to exercise. If one is added, the sandbox needs a database service and this manifest an amendment.

not_exercised.what: Clock-dependent behaviour: the ?on= default (LocalDate.now()) is reached when the parameter is omitted, but nothing pins what it should return, because the answer changes with the day.
not_exercised.why: Deliberate in the app's design — the rule is tested against a day passed in. A test of the default would have to inject a clock, which the app has no seam for.

not_exercised.what: Any configuration binding. There is no src/main/resources, no application.properties and no @Value or System.getenv anywhere in src, so no configuration path is exercised beyond Spring's own SERVER_PORT.
not_exercised.why: Nothing in the repo reads configuration. A change that introduces config will need the variable added here.

not_exercised.what: Packaging and release beyond mvn package: no container image is built, nothing is published, and the jar is never run as java -jar in the trial.
not_exercised.why: The repo has no Dockerfile, compose file or deploy workflow; spring-boot:run is the documented way to run it.

not_exercised.what: Other JDKs. The sandbox builds with whatever java resolves to on PATH (JDK 25 in the agent container, the runner's default JDK on the runner), while CI pins Temurin 17 and the pom targets release 17.
not_exercised.why: The sandbox's environment is closed and does not set JAVA_HOME, so a JDK-version regression that only shows on 17 would not be caught here; CI still covers it.

not_exercised.what: Any checker beyond the compiler. javac -Xlint finds what the compiler already knows at the source level — raw types, unchecked casts, fall-through, deprecation — and nothing else. No SpotBugs, PMD or ErrorProne, so no dataflow or bug-pattern analysis; no spotless or checkstyle, so formatting and style are unchecked.
not_exercised.why: The pom declares no linter, formatter or analysis plugin, and the instruction is not to add a tool the repo does not use. javac is the one checker this build genuinely runs, so it is the one wired to the static gate. The rule pack declares pmd and spotless as well; hardening adds them to the pom when a change needs them, and this manifest then wants another amendment.

not_exercised.what: Coverage of the test sources themselves, and branch coverage as a gate number. JaCoCo instruments only what the build compiles into target/classes, so a changed file under src/test/java has no entry in the report and contributes nothing to diff coverage. Branch data is carried in the lcov as BRDA lines, but the gate counts lines.
not_exercised.why: Normal for JaCoCo and for the gate's line-based diff coverage; recorded so a PR that only touches tests is understood to be unmeasurable rather than uncovered.

not_exercised.what: Both new commands in this agent container end to end against Maven Central itself: Central answered 404 with a retry-after of about 8.6 hours to every request from this runner's egress IP for the whole round.
not_exercised.why: An egress-reputation block, not a repo fact. Everything was verified instead through Google's byte-for-byte Central mirror, configured in a settings file under /tmp and passed via MAVEN_ARGS, so the manifest's own commands and egress list are unchanged and still point at Central. If the block reaches the runner too, the install step fails first and the trial says so.

static_checks.name: javac-lint
static_checks.command:
rm -rf target/static target/bsf-javac && mkdir -p target/static target/bsf-javac && JV=$(grep -o '<java.version>[^<]*' pom.xml | head -1 | cut -d'>' -f2) && mvn -B -ntp org.apache.maven.plugins:maven-dependency-plugin:3.6.1:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile=target/bsf-classpath.txt -Dmdep.includeScope=test && javac -Xlint:all --release "${JV:-17}" -proc:none -d target/bsf-javac -cp "$(cat target/bsf-classpath.txt)" $(find src -name '*.java') > target/bsf-javac.log 2>&1; python3 -I - target/bsf-javac.log target/static/javac.sarif <<'PY'
import json, os, re, sys
src, dst = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
text = open(src, errors="replace").read()
if re.search(r"^.*\.java:\d+: error: ", text, re.M) or re.search(r"^error: ", text, re.M):
    sys.exit("javac reported compilation errors; not writing SARIF")
pat = re.compile(r"^(\S.*?\.java):(\d+): warning: (?:\[([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\] )?(.*)$")
results, rules = [], {}
for line in text.splitlines():
    m = pat.match(line)
    if not m:
        continue
    rule = m.group(3) or "javac"
    rules[rule] = True
    results.append({"ruleId": rule, "level": "warning",
                    "message": {"text": m.group(4).strip()},
                    "locations": [{"physicalLocation": {
                        "artifactLocation": {"uri": m.group(1).replace(os.sep, "/")},
                        "region": {"startLine": int(m.group(2))}}}]})
log = {"version": "2.1.0",
       "$schema": "https://json.schemastore.org/sarif-2.1.0.json",
       "runs": [{"tool": {"driver": {"name": "javac",
                                     "informationUri": "https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/17/docs/specs/man/javac.html",
                                     "rules": [{"id": r, "name": r} for r in sorted(rules)]}},
                 "results": results}]}
os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dst) or ".", exist_ok=True)
json.dump(log, open(dst, "w"), indent=1)
print("wrote %s: %d finding(s) across %d rule(s)" % (dst, len(results), len(rules)))
PY
static_checks.why: The repo's own checker. .factory/rules/java.yaml names javac-lint as this language's linter — the compiler's own -Xlint warnings, which need nothing installed and which a developer can reproduce with the JDK they already have — and the factory has no built-in Java checker, so without this entry the static gate counts nothing on every PR. The command builds the test-scope classpath with Maven, compiles every source under src/ with -Xlint:all at the pom's own java.version, and turns each `file:line: warning: [category]` into a SARIF result whose ruleId is the lint category, which is what the gate counts per rule per file. It writes no SARIF when javac reports compilation errors, so a broken classpath is reported as unavailable rather than as a clean repo.
